downloadedSourceCountNote: No download occurred. Five originals were supplied by the project owner as a human-input drop and measured under external read-only custody. A supplied file is not an acquisition and does not create a retrieval receipt.

method.measurement: Every value below was recomputed from the supplied bytes. Nothing was carried over from a prior record or from a filename.

forms.officialTitle: Petitioner’s Instructions for Expungement (Sealing) of Criminal Records
forms.note: The form carries a printed revision, so no revision is unknown and none was invented. It names EXP102, EXP105, EXP106 and EXP107 as the forms it instructs on.

forms.officialTitle: Notice of Hearing and Petition for Expungement
forms.note: Its own face directs the participant to EXP101 for help completing it, which corroborates the instructions pairing.

Its printed caption is "Proof of Service (EXP104)", so it is an EXP-family document and its own face says so. It carries "Rev 1/25" in the page footer, twice. This is the newest revision in the set — every other form here reads 7/24 or 1/24.
forms.mn55xxStringsAreAddressees: The MN 5510, 5515 and 5516 strings on this face are the addressee codes of the agencies served — the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension and its counterparts — not a form-family designation. They appear in the service list a participant checks off, which is what a proof of service is for.

embeddedMetadataTitleIsWrong.embeddedTitle: Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records (Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3)
embeddedMetadataTitleIsWrong.finding: The PDF's own document-properties Title names subd. 3, which is EXP105's route, not this form's. The printed face is right and the embedded metadata is stale — the file was almost certainly produced from the EXP105 template. Recorded because a resolver reading document properties instead of the face would bind EXP106 to the subd. 3 route and produce an order under the wrong statutory authority. The printed face governs.

separateOrderIdentities.finding: EXP105 and EXP106 are separate proposed orders for separate statutory routes and are kept as separate identities. They share one printed caption — "Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records" — and are told apart by the statute printed directly beneath it: EXP105 cites Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3, and EXP106 cites subd. 1 or 2. That is the route difference stated on the documents themselves rather than inferred from a numbering convention.
separateOrderIdentities.measurementCorroboration: The measurement independently supports two documents rather than two copies of one: different page counts (4 against 3), different byte counts, different digests, and different printed revisions — EXP105 reads Rev 7/24 and EXP106 reads Rev 1/24. A single document could not carry two revisions.
separateOrderIdentities.titleAloneCannotDistinguishThem: Because the captions are identical, any resolver selecting by title would find both and could bind either. Selection must carry the statutory subdivision. EXP106's embedded PDF Title makes this worse by naming subd. 3, so document properties are an actively wrong discriminator here.

signerClassification.note: A proposed order is drafted by the participant and signed by the court. It is participant-facing and is not participant-signed, and the packet must not present it as something the participant executes.
signerClassification.exp104Note: EXP104 is signed by whoever mailed the documents, which its face states as "I, (name of person who mailed the documents)". That is participant-side but not necessarily the petitioner, so it is recorded as its own class rather than folded into participantSigned.

structuralObservation: Four of the five are flat PDFs with no AcroForm at all, so the renderer lane for the EXP family is flat_pdf_overlay and not acroform_fill. EXP104 reports a clean_acroform structure with zero terminal fields, which is an AcroForm dictionary carrying no fields and is not fillable either. No lane is assigned here.

supersessionAssessment.reason: The adopted edition manifests no EXP-family binary for Minnesota, so there is no retained byte string for these to supersede. These are first measurements, not replacements.

licensing.basis: No Minnesota reuse or commercial-use term was supplied with the drop and none is asserted on the measured faces. Possession of a form is not permission to reproduce it.
licensing.owner: rcap-mn-written-permission-authorization or counsel, if the Minnesota licence question is raised

sourceContractAndMaterialization.reason: A source receipt requires an exact authorized source contract. The Minnesota identities are measured exactly but their licence position is unresolved and their canonical identities are not yet admitted to an edition, so no receipt is created. The evidence is retained under external read-only custody instead, which is custody without permission and is exactly the distinction the Colorado work established.

terminalDispositionDetail: The currentness comparison is answered for all five forms from their own printed revisions: EXP101 Rev 7/24, EXP102 Rev 7/24, EXP104 Rev 1/25, EXP105 Rev 7/24, EXP106 Rev 1/24. No revision was invented and none was carried over from a filename or a prior record.
expectedDownstreamEffect: Minnesota moves from an unretrieved attended-retrieval assignment to five exactly measured identities held under hash-verified external custody, with the two proposed orders preserved as distinct identities and the renderer question answered by measurement rather than assumption. No receipt is created, no binary enters version control, no component is rebound, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.

measurementCorrections.why: The first pass recorded EXP104 as printing no revision. It prints one, in the page footer, on both pages. The value is read from the face.

The caption was left as a placeholder and the accompanying note inferred, from the MN 5510/5515/5516 strings, that the form might belong to the MN 55xx family rather than the EXP family. Those strings are the agencies being served. The printed caption reads "Proof of Service (EXP104)" and settles both questions.

measurementCorrections.was: descriptive paraphrases ("Petition to Expunge Criminal Records", "route one", "route two")
measurementCorrections.nowIs: the exact printed captions, with the statute printed beneath each
measurementCorrections.why: A paraphrase cannot be matched against an official face, and "route one"/"route two" encoded the conclusion instead of the evidence for it. The two orders share a caption and are separated by their statutory subdivision, which is now recorded on each row.

residualBlockers.question: Whether Minnesota asserts any reuse restriction over its court forms.
residualBlockers.why: Nothing in the supplied drop speaks to reuse. Silence is not permission.

residualBlockers.question: None of the five is admitted to an adopted edition, so no component may bind them yet.
